arxiv-2011-13846.title: Persuading a Wishful Thinker Thanks: We especially thank Jeanne Hagenbach and Eduardo Perez-Richet for their comments and support. We also thank S. Nageeb Ali, Sarah Auster, Gregorio Curello, Roland Bénabou, Geoffroy de Clippel, Alexis Ghersengorin, Simon Gleyze, Emeric Henry, Deniz Kattwinkel, Fréd
arxiv-2011-13846.creator: Victor Augias, Daniel M. A. Barreto
arxiv-2011-13846.description: Abstract We study a persuasion problem in which a sender designs an information structure to induce a non-Bayesian receiver to take a particular action. The receiver, who is privately informed about his preferences, is a wishful thinker: he is systematically overoptimistic about the most favorable outcomes.

arxiv-2012-13799.title: Hyperheavy spherical and toroidal nuclei: the role of shell structure.
arxiv-2012-13799.creator: S. E. Agbemava, A. V. Afanasjev
arxiv-2012-13799.description: Abstract The properties of toroidal hyperheavy even-even nuclei and the role of toroidal shell structure are extensively studied within covariant density functional theory. The general trends in the evolution of toroidal shapes in the Z ≈ 130 − 180 Z\approx 130-180 region of nuclear chart are established for the first time. These nuclei are stable with respect of breathing deformations.

arxiv-2109-11455.title: Multi-angle Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
arxiv-2109-11455.creator: Rebekah Herrman, Phillip C. Lotshaw, James Ostrowski, Travis S. Humble, George Siopsis
arxiv-2109-11455.description: Abstract The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) generates an approximate solution to combinatorial optimization problems using a variational ansatz circuit defined by parameterized layers of quantum evolution. In theory, the approximation improves with increasing ansatz depth but gate noise and circuit complexity undermine performance in practice.

arxiv-2302-11951.title: Pixel Difference Convolutional Network for RGB-D Semantic Segmentation
arxiv-2302-11951.creator: Jun Yang, Lizhi Bai, Yaoru Sun, Chunqi Tian, Maoyu Mao, Guorun Wang
arxiv-2302-11951.description: Abstract RGB-D semantic segmentation can be advanced with convolutional neural networks due to the availability of Depth data. Although objects cannot be easily discriminated by just the 2D appearance, with the local pixel difference and geometric patterns in Depth, they can be well separated in some cases.

arxiv-2304-00577.title: Stochastic Multiple Fields Inflation: Diffusion Dominated Regime
arxiv-2304-00577.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . We study multiple fields inflation in diffusion dominated regime using stochastic δ ​ N \delta N formalism. The fields are under pure Brownian motion in a dS background with boundaries in higher dimensional field space. This setup can be realized towards the final stages of the ultra slow-roll setup where the classical drifts fall off exponentially and the perturbations are driven by quantum kicks.

arxiv-2306-02465.title: Overview of the JWST Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey (JADES)
arxiv-2306-02465.creator: Daniel J. Eisenstein, Chris Willott, Stacey Alberts, Santiago Arribas, Nina Bonaventura, Andrew J. Bunker, Alex J. Cameron, Stefano Carniani, Stephane Charlot, Emma Curtis-Lake, Francesco D’Eugenio, Pierre Ferruit, Giovanna Giardino, Kevin Hainline, Ryan Hausen, Peter Jakobsen, Benjamin D. Johnson,
arxiv-2306-02465.description: Abstract We present an overview of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey (JADES), an ambitious program of infrared imaging and spectroscopy in the GOODS-S and GOODS-N deep fields, designed to study galaxy evolution from high redshift to cosmic noon.

arxiv-2404-03489.title: Design of Stickbug: a Six-Armed Precision Pollination Robot Thanks: 1 The authors are with the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, West Virginia University, Morgantown, WV 26505, USA Thanks: 2 Trevor Smith is the corresponding author trs0024@mix.wvu.edu Thanks: This study was support
arxiv-2404-03489.creator: Jared Beard, R. Tyler Cook, Andy Chu, Jason Gross, Yu Gu West Virginia University Morgantown, USA
arxiv-2404-03489.description: Abstract This work presents the design of Stickbug, a six-armed, multi-agent, precision pollination robot that combines the accuracy of single-agent systems with swarm parallelization in greenhouses. Precision pollination robots have often been proposed to offset the effects of a decreasing population of natural pollinators, but they frequently lack the required parallelization and scalability.

arxiv-2405-11403.title: MapCoder : Multi-Agent Code Generation for Competitive Problem Solving
arxiv-2405-11403.creator: Md. Ashraful Islam, Mohammed Eunus Ali, Md Rizwan Parvez
arxiv-2405-11403.description: Abstract Code synthesis, which requires a deep understanding of complex natural language (NL) problem descriptions, generation of code instructions for complex algorithms and data structures, and the successful execution of comprehensive unit tests, presents a significant challenge. Thus, while large language models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive proficiency in natural language processing (NLP), their performance in code generation tasks remains limited.

arxiv-2503-21869.description: Abstract We have not yet observed the epoch at which disc galaxies emerge in the Universe. While high- z z measurements of large-scale features such as bars and spiral arms trace the evolution of disc galaxies, such methods cannot directly quantify featureless discs in the early Universe.

arxiv-2510-18335.title: Support growth of vorticity for bi-rotational Euler flows in high dimensions
arxiv-2510-18335.creator: In-Jee Jeong, Deokwoo Lim
arxiv-2510-18335.description: Abstract . We study incompressible Euler equations in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} with d ≥ 4 d\geq 4 under bi-rotational symmetry without swirl, which reduces the Euler equations to a scalar vorticity advection in the first quadrant. We show that patch type initial vorticities exhibit infinite growth of the support diameter.

arxiv-2512-24165.title: DiffThinker: Towards Generative Multimodal Reasoning with Diffusion Models
arxiv-2512-24165.creator: Zefeng He, Xiaoye Qu, Yafu Li, Tong Zhu, Siyuan Huang, Yu Cheng
arxiv-2512-24165.description: Abstract While recent Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have attained significant strides in multimodal reasoning, their reasoning processes remain predominantly text-centric, leading to suboptimal performance in complex long-horizon, vision-centric tasks. In this paper, we establish a novel Generative Multimodal Reasoning paradigm and introduce DiffThinker, a diffusion-based reasoning framework.
